review.summary: Reviewed bench/mod.rs, bench/local.rs and soak.rs for input parsing, DoS and resource bounds. The client-side reads of peer data are mostly bounded: the upload refusal reply is read with a 4096-byte cap and a 10 s timeout, the local relay HTTP probe is capped at 1024 bytes under a 5 s timeout, and concurrency workers are bounded by --concurrency-size. Two hypotheses remain, both depending on golem-p2p code that is not in the supplied files.

findings.title: Echo reply from a malicious listener is buffered without a size check before the byte comparison
findings.prerequisites: A malicious peer that the operator benchmarks with `bench --to`, and whose reply to an echo request is larger than the request. The golem-p2p request path must not cap reply size, which this file does not show.
findings.impact: If `ep.request` does not cap the reply, a malicious listener can make the client allocate its whole reply in memory before the `ends_with` check. Concurrency runs up to 64 streams, so the allocation multiplies by the stream count.
findings.evidence: let reply = ep.request(to, &payload).await?; if !reply.ends_with(&payload) { bail!("unexpected reply"); }
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the reply cap in golem-p2p's request implementation. If it is absent or larger than the request size, cap replies at the request size plus a small margin. Compare the length first and reject oversized replies before buffering.
findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis, not demonstrated. Run a test listener that answers a 64-byte request with a 1 GiB reply and measure the client's peak RSS. The same test applies to the soak requester at soak.rs:348.

findings.title: Lookup-time map keyed by peer id grows with every lookup and is never pruned
findings.prerequisites: The endpoint calls `Discovery::lookup` for node IDs that the peer chooses, for example identities taken from incoming connections or relay-compare traffic. The source given here does not show that path.
findings.impact: The map gains one entry per distinct node ID looked up. Those IDs can be attacker-chosen, so a peer that causes many lookups makes the map grow without bound for the life of the bench run. The run is short, so the impact is limited.
findings.suggested_fix: Store only the lookup time for the `to` node and the relay-compare node, or cap the map size and evict. Alternatively keep only the most recent lookup for `to`.
findings.validation_needed: Hypothesis. Check whether golem-p2p calls Discovery::lookup for inbound or attacker-supplied IDs. If it does, count map entries after a run in which a peer triggers many such lookups.

limitations: golem-p2p's request, reply-size and connection code is not in the supplied files, so the reply-size bound for ep.request cannot be confirmed.
Whether the endpoint looks up peer-supplied node IDs through the Discovery trait is not shown.
Path-change and PathLog growth, and Pinger sample accumulation (probe module), are not in the supplied files.
The HTTP directory client's response body limit (HttpDirectory::lookup) is outside the supplied code. Directories are operator-configured, so they fall under the trusted-operator assumption.
Tests were reviewed for their content only; they were not run.
